name: From one's own work to entering the Lord (BhG 18.45–56)

stages.name: sva-karman as worship
stages.description: Devoted to his own action, a man finds perfection by worshipping with it the one from whom beings proceed; one's own dharma is not to be abandoned (18.45–48).

stages.name: naiṣkarmya-siddhi
stages.gloss: the perfection of freedom from action
stages.description: Understanding unattached everywhere, self-conquered, free of longing, one attains it through renunciation (18.49).

stages.name: fitness for becoming brahman
stages.description: Purified understanding, restraint by steadfastness, giving up sense-objects, passion and aversion, solitude, light food, restraint of speech, body and mind, constant meditation, dispassion, and casting off ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possession, without 'mine', at peace (18.51–53).

stages.name: brahma-bhūta
stages.description: Serene, neither grieving nor desiring, the same to all beings (18.54).

stages.name: parā bhakti
stages.description: He attains supreme devotion, and by devotion knows the Lord in truth (18.54–55).

stages.name: entering the Lord
stages.description: Having known him in truth he enters him immediately thereafter (18.55); one who acts while taking refuge in him attains the eternal abode by his grace (18.56).

notes: Extractor B: stage order as the text gives it; bands are left to the interpretation layer. 18.56 may be read as a parallel route (acting while depending on the Lord) rather than a further stage.
